source: MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture, banana cultivation techniques manual, 2019, section III.1 (sucker selection for planting)
text:
Good planting material is the foundation of a healthy banana plot, and the manual sets out clear criteria for choosing suckers:

- Choose suckers that are visibly healthy, free of disease symptoms and free of pest damage, with firm, undamaged corm tissue.
- Preferred sucker height at digging is roughly 40-100cm.
- "Sword suckers" — offshoots with narrow, upright, sword-shaped leaves — are preferred over broad-leaved "water suckers," because sword suckers generally establish and fruit more reliably.
- The corm should be firm and hard to the touch; soft or hollow-feeling corms should be rejected.
- When cutting a sucker away from the mother clump, cut cleanly with a sharp, disinfected tool, then trim off old roots and any dried or damaged leaf material so the sucker is clean and easy to transport as a single unit.
- If suckers must be dug and planted during the dry season, dip the corm in water before planting to rehydrate it.
- If a batch of suckers cannot be planted immediately, cure them by storing in a shaded, moderately humid spot (the source cites a storage temperature range of roughly 35-40°C) for about 10-15 days to let cut wounds heal and reduce disease risk before planting.
- Suckers should ideally be planted within about one week of being dug, to avoid excessive drying or rot of the cut surface.
- Where possible, plant suckers from the same batch/age together, since suckers with 2-3 leaves at digging establish and grow more uniformly, making later field management and harvest timing easier across the plot.
